newsitem.title: USA: U.S July consumer credit rose $7.7 billion.
newsitem.headline: U.S July consumer credit rose $7.7 billion.

text.p: U.S. consumer installment credit rose $7.7 billion in July at an eight percent annual rate, after increasing a revised $6.7 billion in June at a seven percent annual rate, the Federal Reserve said Monday.
Previously, the Fed said June consumer credit outstanding had risen much more strongly by $8.3 billion but it revised that estimate down.
Wall Street analysts had forecast that July consumer credit would grow by $7.2 billion.
Growth in auto credit outstanding slowed in July to a $1.9 billion increase at a 6.3 percent annual rate from a June rise of $5.6 billion at an 18.5 percent annual rate.
But revolving or credit-card debt in July jumped $7.2 billion at a 19.4 percent annual rate, compared with a $2.1 billion June gain at a 5.7 percent annual rate.

Other credit, which includes consumer bank loans but not real estate mortgages, decreased for a fourth straight month, falling $1.5 billion at a 5.1 percent annual rate in July. This credit category had declined by $900,000 in June at a 3.5 percent annual rate.
Before seasonal adjustment, total outstanding consumer credit in July was $1.154 trillion, up from $1.149 trillion in June and up from $1.039 trillion in July 1995.
